Task ID: T11
Title: Create city-level Eurostat analytical matrix
Family: analytics

Pivot Eurostat long-format indicator data into a city-year by indicator matrix.

Available input files:
- outputs/t02_eurostat_raw.csv

Required output files:
- outputs/t11_city_indicator_matrix.csv

Output requirements:
- outputs/t11_city_indicator_matrix.csv:
  - CSV identifier columns: city_id, city_name, year
  - Include one column for every indicator_id in outputs/t02_eurostat_raw.csv.
  - Use one row per city_id/year pair.

import pandas as pd

# Read the raw Eurostat data
input_file = "outputs/t02_eurostat_raw.csv"
output_file = "outputs/t11_city_indicator_matrix.csv"

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv(input_file)

# Identify the unique indicator IDs to ensure we have columns for all of them
indicator_ids = df['indicator_id'].unique()

# Pivot the data
# We assume the long format has columns like: city_id, city_name, year, indicator_id, value
# We pivot to have indicator_id as columns and the value as the cell content
pivoted_df = df.pivot_table(
    index=['city_id', 'city_name', 'year'],
    columns='indicator_id',
    values='value',
    aggfunc='first'  # In case of duplicates, take the first value
).reset_index()

# Reorder columns to ensure identifier columns come first, followed by indicator columns
# The required order is: city_id, city_name, year, then all indicator_ids
cols = ['city_id', 'city_name', 'year'] + sorted(indicator_ids)

# Ensure all columns exist (in case some indicators have no data for any city)
for col in indicator_ids:
    if col not in pivoted_df.columns:
        pivoted_df[col] = None

# Reorder and select only the required columns
pivoted_df = pivoted_df[cols]

# Save to CSV
pivoted_df.to_csv(output_file, index=False)

print(f"Successfully created {output_file}")
</solution_file>
